summary: SRanger controller implemented in package sranger (9 Java files): one controller with modes MOVING/TURNING/FINAL, six step() transitions plus the initial mode, a timed Turning -> Moving transition through a Clock-based clockResetTime, an IR Sensor, a recording Actuator and a single two-component Move output event. All 23 requirements are traced. Nine points the requirements did not settle are listed below; none blocks the pipeline.

issues.title: Sensor.distance() default when no reading is available: 1000.0 m
issues.raw: SR-DM5: 'When no reading is available ... distance() returns a large default value so that the obstacle-detection condition is not falsely triggered.' No value is given.
issues.fix_directive: Chose NO_READING_DISTANCE = 1000.0 m (far above obstacleThreshold 0.5 m). update() also treats a negative, NaN or > 1000 m measurement as 'no reading', which keeps distance() non-negative (SR-SF1). If a different sentinel is wanted, change NO_READING_DISTANCE in Sensor.java; nothing else depends on its value.

issues.title: Actuator's recorded command before any command is (0.0, 0.0)
issues.raw: SR-DM6: 'The Actuator ... stores the latest issued command.' The value before the first command is not given.
issues.fix_directive: Initialised lastLinearVelocity and lastAngularVelocity to 0.0 (stationary). In practice the controller constructor issues Move(moveVel, 0) immediately, so the default is only observable before a controller is attached.

issues.title: Move is one event record with two real components, sent via actuator.apply(...)
issues.raw: SR-DM4: 'a single output event, Move, carrying two real values — a linear velocity and an angular velocity.' The profile's event guidance describes events with one component.
issues.fix_directive: Implemented OutputEvent.Move(double lv, double av) and emit it as actuator.apply(new OutputEvent.Move(lv, av)). The alternative (one component of a Velocity datatype) was rejected because the requirement names two real values, not a type. If the pipeline cannot type a two-component event, switch to a Velocity record payload.

issues.title: Moving's entry command at power-up is issued in the controller constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1: 'Moving is the initial mode on power-up ... on entering Moving, the controller issues Move(moveVel, 0).' SR-Beh1: 'On power-up, the SRanger controller begins in Moving.' step() carries transitions only, so it cannot express the initial entry.
issues.fix_directive: The constructor issues Move(MOVE_VEL, 0.0) after wiring its collaborators; without it the robot would sit still in Moving. The extracted model's initial transition may not carry this action; that affects only the first output, not deadlock or divergence.

issues.title: Moving -> Turning uses both the obstacle event and the obstacleDetected guard
issues.raw: SR-Beh2: 'transitions from Moving to Turning when the obstacle event is received.' SR-GP1: 'obstacleDetected (distance <= obstacleThreshold) ... is used as the guard on the Moving -> Turning transition.'
issues.fix_directive: Implemented as trigger Obstacle with guard obstacleDetected (both requirements honoured). Consequence: an obstacle event that arrives while the latest reading is above the threshold (or absent) is ignored and the robot keeps Moving.

issues.title: Turning priority: endTask, then the timed return, then tick
issues.raw: SR-Beh5 (autonomous Turning -> Moving), SR-Beh6 (endTask), SR-Beh7 (tick self-loop) give no relative priority.
issues.fix_directive: endTask is first, as the stop that overrides everything. The autonomous turnDurationElapsed transition comes before the tick self-loop; otherwise a tick every cycle would keep the robot turning forever. The tick branch conjoins !turnDurationElapsed as the profile requires. The tick self-loops (SR-Beh4, SR-Beh7) perform no action, and in particular do not reset clockResetTime. In Java the return to Moving happens at the first step() at or after turnDuration, so it is quantised to the control cycle.

issues.title: OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 is fractional and is rounded up to 1 in the model
issues.raw: SR-DM2: obstacleThreshold default 0.5 m. The model's constants interface rounds a fractional constant up to the next integer, and this constant appears in the obstacleDetected guard.
issues.fix_directive: Kept the requirement's unit (metres) and value 0.5 as a plain decimal literal. Rescaling everything to centimetres would change SR-DM5/SR-SF1's unit. In the extracted model the guard therefore reads distance() <= 1. Deadlock and divergence results are unaffected, but any model-level property about the exact detection distance is coarser than the Java. The other three constants (1.0, 2.0, 2.0) are integral and exact.

issues.title: Time base is a framework-advanced Clock; the controller field is named timer
issues.raw: SR-Var1: clockResetTime records 'the current time'. The requirements do not say where time comes from.
issues.fix_directive: Clock.now() returns seconds and advance(seconds) moves it forward monotonically; the framework that delivers tick advances it each cycle. This is deterministic and testable; a wall-clock implementation could replace the body of now(). The controller field is named timer because clock is a RoboChart reserved word. clockResetTime starts at 0.0 and is only read in Turning, after it has been set.

issues.title: Events no requirement handles are ignored; Final has no outgoing transition
issues.raw: No requirement gives a transition for obstacle in Turning, or for any event in Final. SR-FR3: 'Final is the terminal mode.' SR-DC1: each SR-Beh maps to exactly one transition.
issues.fix_directive: No extra transitions were invented: obstacle in Turning is ignored, apart from the autonomous check that runs on every step. Final's block is empty, a terminal mode (time still passes there in RoboChart). If a verifier needs Final to accept tick, add a Final -> Final tick self-loop. No requirement asks for one.
